taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Ulakwo, Etche LGA survey stations. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 14.369 | 0.124 | 0.12415
2 | 15.965 | 8.25 | 9.665
3 | 4591.4 | 27.074 | 47.738
4 | 5101.5 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as HA-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Ulakwo, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Station Ulakwo, Etche LGA**

The VES interpretation at Ulakwo resolved four layers. Layer 1 (14.369 Ω·m, 0.124 m thick) is a thin, low-resistivity topsoil. Layer 2 (15.965 Ω·m, 8.25 m thick) shows a slight resistivity increase, consistent with weathered/lateritic material. Layer 3 (4591.4 Ω·m, 27.07 m thick) marks a sharp resistivity rise, likely a competent sand/gravel or fractured basement unit. Layer 4 (5101.5 Ω·m, inferred as the basal layer) continues the increasing resistivity trend, suggesting resistive basement or consolidated formation at depth.

Checking the resistivity progression: r1 < r2 < r3 gives "A", and r2 < r3 < r4 also gives "A". The sequence is therefore continuously increasing with depth, which corresponds to curve type **A**, not the HA-type recorded on file. The filed classification does not match the tabulated resistivity values and should be corrected.

{"curve_type_stated": "HA", "label_issue_flagged": true}
